chapter: Stuff Smith stories, Wes Montgomery and singers
title: Stuff Smith, Jonah Jones and the suspended union cards
summary: Retelling how Stuff went back to Buffalo to see his wife and the whole group was suspended for a year.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Did he do any other improvisations like that to get what he wanted, that you can remember?
Oh, yes. Now, that -- let's see -- when it was Jonah Jones and Stuff Smith, this was years before our time, you know, before John Levy and I joined it.
Uh-huh.
They were working here in California, I think it was a yacht club or some club named after a 52nd Street club.
Uh-huh.

And these guys used to get in a car and always ride to work in the car. It was out here in Hollywood somewhere. And so they waited for Stuff and he didn't show up, and they came to work, he never did show up, Stuff had taken a train back to Buffalo.
(Laughter)
To see his wife. He missed his wife,

and instead of sending for her he just turned around and went back to see her. And it brought everybody up -- it made a federal case out of it, and the guys were suspended for a year, and it was Stuff's fault, because they had Cozy Cole, Clyde Hart, I think Al Hall, Jonah Jones. They had guys that were quite prominent in those days, you know?
And the whole group got suspended because of what Stuff did.
Yeah. Well, he broke the contract.
Uh-huh.
And Stuff just felt like going back to see his wife. On the spur of the moment. He would do those kinds of things, you know.
(Laughter)
You mentioned that the "My People," album was recorded sometime after the show was over.
Yes.
Where was it recorded?
In Chicago.
In Chicago?
Yeah, we all went back to Chicago to record it.
